chapter: Freelance and studio work in New York
title: Dick Himber's Studebaker Champions with Artie Shaw
summary: He arranged for Himber's group, which featured Shaw's subtone clarinet and a string section.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Oh, I worked for Dick Himber, I did a lot of things for Dick Himber on that little group he had called Studebaker Champion. Artie Shaw, was -- he played the subtone clarinet.
Richard Himber, there was Jack Sadey, Sleninsky, the guy that traveled around with the Boston Symphony with Bazhinsky (all phonetics) Freddie Fradkin and somebody else. They had four fiddles.
And Shaw was playing the clarinet.
Shaw was playing the subtone. He only played a chorus. Berley Middles, Arnold Brillhart's wife, played the harp and then we used whatever saxophones or whatever clarinets in the band.
I guess you knew Shaw from around New York anyway.
Oh, yeah, had him -- got Nat to use him, as a side man. He played our -- he was our first saxophone player. This is when he was -- we used to go out and listen to bands together.
